lyrics:
[Intro: hand drums and a scraped gourd, friends talking, a laugh]
Otra, otra

[Verse 1: warm, low, half sung over hand drums]
Dominoes slapping on a folding table
Somebody's cousin fixing someone's cable
The radio's old and the beer is warm
And I had no idea that this was the whole thing

[Pre-Chorus: bass enters, voice lifts]
I took the sunset
I took the sea
I never took the people next to me

[Chorus: crowd of friends singing, full percussion]
Should have taken one more picture
Of the nothing-special days
Uncle sleeping in the lawn chair
Grandma's hands, the way she prays
Otra foto, otra foto
Before the light went low
I've got a thousand of the sunsets
And none of the people I know

[Verse 2: warm, a little faster]
Half of the block moved north for the money
Half of the rest went quiet and funny
The corner store's a place that sells candles now
And I'd give it all back for one loud afternoon

[Pre-Chorus: bass and voice lift]
I took the skyline
I took the food
I never took the room with all of you

[Chorus: crowd of friends singing, full percussion]
Should have taken one more picture
Of the nothing-special days
Uncle sleeping in the lawn chair
Grandma's hands, the way she prays
Otra foto, otra foto
Before the light went low
I've got a thousand of the sunsets
And none of the people I know

[Bridge: drums and voices only, Spanish, clapping]
Quédate un ratito más
(Quédate, quédate)
Mi gente, mi barrio
(Otra foto, por favor)

[Final Chorus: everyone, horns join, shouting and laughing]
Should have taken one more picture
Of the nothing-special days
Uncle sleeping in the lawn chair
Grandma's hands, the way she prays
Otra foto, otra foto
Before the light went low
So everybody get together
Now, before you go

[Outro: hand drums, a camera shutter, cheering]
Otra
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 136 BPM, 4/4, A major. A lively street-party rhythm with a wistful melody over it. Joy and ache together.

VOICE: Male, warm, low and relaxed, half singing and half speaking in a conversational murmur, with a Caribbean Spanish accent on the Spanish lines. The choruses are sung by a loose crowd of friends, men and women, not polished, with laughter and shouts left in.

INSTRUMENTS: Hand-held frame drums in interlocking patterns (the plena rhythm). A scraped gourd. A deep, simple bass with a light reggaeton kick underneath. Bright synth chords. A small horn section in the last chorus. Handclaps. Party ambience and a camera shutter.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, hand drums, voices and a laugh. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:36 Pre-chorus. 0:48 Chorus 1, the crowd. 1:16 Verse 2. 1:40 Pre-chorus. 1:52 Chorus 2. 2:20 Bridge in Spanish over drums and clapping. 2:36 Final chorus with horns, the last two lines changed. 3:04 Outro, drums, a shutter click and cheering at 3:16.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2020s Latin pop rooted in folk percussion: warm, live-sounding and crowded, drums and voices close, as if recorded in a back yard.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The crowd entering on the first chorus at 0:48.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The last chorus stops regretting and gives an instruction: everybody get together, now. That is the lesson people over fifty took from the original, and the shutter at the end is someone acting on it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Fond memory, regret, longing, a group photograph.
